title: Lesson 22: Cost Management: Token Budgets, Model Tiers, and Predictable Client Pricing
description: Measuring what a single run costs, routing reasoning and mechanical work onto the right model tiers, keeping recurring workloads inside a budget, and turning a measured unit cost into predictable client pricing.

questions.question: Per the lesson about cost management, what is the central focus?
options: A review of unrelated spreadsheet tools
Measuring unit cost, putting each piece of work on the right model tier, budgeting recurring load, and pricing the engagement from measurement
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches how to make the number measured and turn a measured unit cost into a client number that survives the month.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson's guidance?
options: Price the engagement from token math you have not observed
Leave every auxiliary task on auto so summarization runs on the premium model
A five-minute health check should run as an agent job for reliability
Measure a week of real runs before you put a number in a proposal, and never price from a demo
questions.explanation: The lesson is explicit that a three-run demo tells you nothing, so you measure a week of real runs before pricing.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support?
options: Model choice is the largest cost difference in a long-running agent
The cache is the biggest cost lever because a mid-session model switch re-reads the whole context at full price
Switching models mid-conversation is always cheap
Inference is the largest cost of the engagement and should drive the price
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that the cache is the biggest single lever, since a switch mid-conversation discards the cached prefix and re-reads the full context at full price.
